title: Atypical Alzheimer disease: a multi-axis framework toward defining heterogeneity
title_zh: 典型阿尔茨海默病：定义异质性的多轴框架
abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is defined biologically by the presence of amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques and tau neurofibrillary tangles in the brain; however, these pathologies do not affect all brain regions equally. Typical AD usually presents with memory impairment, whereas atypical forms of AD, including posterior cortical atrophy, logopenic variant primary progressive aphasia, behavioural and dysexecutive AD, and corticobasal syndrome, manifest with prominent non-memory symptoms. Aβ biomarkers usually confirm that AD pathology is present, whereas regional tau, neurodegeneration and dysfunction more closely track the affected network and the presenting symptoms. The atypical variants, which tend to present at a younger age than typical AD, provide human models to study selective vulnerability of neurons and circuits. They also help us to test whether immune–glial, vascular, protein-handling, synaptic or genetic factors shape regional vulnerability and rate of progression beyond total Aβ and tau burden. In this Review, we integrate clinical, neuropathological, imaging, genetic and molecular evidence to describe atypical AD within the broader AD spectrum. We propose a practical multi-axis framework comprising clinical phenotype, AD biological context (AD pathology plus co-pathologies and molecular modifiers), network topography (regional patterns) and tempo (rate of clinical and biomarker progression). This framework could reduce diagnostic mismatches, make cohorts more comparable and support trials that include outcomes tailored to the affected brain networks. Atypical Alzheimer disease (AD) denotes cases that meet the neuropathological criteria for AD but manifest predominantly with non-amnestic network failure. In this Review, the authors argue that atypical AD provides a starting point for studying the mechanisms that shape AD heterogeneity, and they propose a practical multi-axis framework to capture this heterogeneity.
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（AD）在生物学上以大脑中β-淀粉样蛋白（Aβ）斑块和tau神经纤维样条的存在为特征；然而，这些病理改变并非均匀影响所有脑区。典型AD通常表现为记忆障碍，而AD的典型亚型，包括后皮质萎缩、进行性顶叶失语症变异型、行为和执行功能障碍型AD以及皮质基底ganglia综合征，则表现为明显的非记忆症状。Aβ生物标志物通常确认AD病理存在，而区域tau、神经退行性变和功能障碍更密切追踪受影响的网络和临床表现。这些亚型倾向于在典型AD发病年龄之前出现，为研究神经元和电路的选择性脆弱性提供了人类模型。它们还有助于我们测试免疫-胶质、血管、蛋白质处理、突触或遗传因素是否在超越总体Aβ和tau负荷的情况下，塑造区域脆弱性和进展速度。在本综述中，我们整合了临床、病理、影像、遗传和分子证据，在更广泛的AD谱系中描述典型AD的亚型。我们提出了一个包含临床表型、AD生物学背景（AD病理加共病和分子修饰）、网络地形（区域模式）和进程速度（临床和生物标志物进展速率）的实用多轴框架。该框架可减少诊断错配，使研究队列更具可比性，并支持针对受影响脑网络结果的临床试验。典型AD（AD）指符合AD病理诊断标准但主要表现为非痴呆性网络功能障碍的病例。在本综述中，作者论述典型AD作为研究AD异质性机制的起点，并提出了一个实用的多轴框架来捕捉这种异质性。
